item.title: Open Source Security at Astral
item.description:
📝 That trust includes confidence in our security posture: developers reasonably expect that our tools (and the processes that build, test, and release them) are secure. Our experience with these triggers is that many projects think that they need them, but the overwhelming majority of their usages are better off being replaced with a less privileged trigger (such as pull_request) or removed entirely. Of course, there are some use cases that do require these triggers, such as anything that does really need to leave comments on third-party issues or pull requests.
🔗 Read more: https://astral.sh/blog/open-source-security-at-astral

item.title: App Store sees 84% surge in new apps as AI coding tools take off
item.description:
📝 “It aligns with a broader release of agentic coding tools that remove prior difficulties of creating apps. In short, some of these apps generate interpreted code that can change their own primary purpose, something Apple does not allow. ” An Apple spokesperson denied that review times are getting longer.
